gaps: The rendered Harry J. Epstein screenshot says “2012–Present,” while its text capture says “2009–2015.” This chronology inconsistency does not defeat PR-015, but it weakens the otherwise coherent professional narrative and should be reconciled.

The resume compresses collective context more aggressively than the project pages, especially by styling Sunday Dinner / 196 as a founder role. The linked case page restores co-organizer and community credit, but that nuance would be safer on the resume itself.

This packet demonstrates careful public-facing boundaries but cannot independently establish underlying image rights, participant consent, or authorization for every derived aggregate. Those remain separate human review gates.
safety_findings: No romanticized vulnerability was observed; trust, care, and cultural-space precarity are framed as operational responsibilities rather than personal spectacle.
Private community records are described but not exposed. The Sunday Dinner reconstructions preserve coordination logic while withholding participant-level values and access details.
Coalition pages repeatedly reject sole causation, sole authorship, attendance inference, endorsement, and publication of protected strategy or stakeholder context.
This pass is observational PR-015 evidence only. It grants no publication, deployment, indexing, testimonial, consent, rights-clearance, or protected-material release authority.
recommendation: Pass PR-015 at score 4 for this exact candidate. Preserve the collective-credit and privacy boundaries, reconcile the Harry J. Epstein chronology, and complete separate human rights and consent review before any publication or deployment decision.
